strings.lock.compressed_text:
This archive is encrypted and compressed. Editing it would mean compressing everything again, which takes hours for a large archive. That is why it stays locked.

Tip: make backups you want to edit in Archy with the 7-Zip compression level Store.
strings.lock.locked_text:
This archive is encrypted and therefore locked, so nothing changes by accident.

Click to unlock it. You can then add, rename and delete files. On Save, Archy writes a new version ({size}) next to the original, with the same password and encrypted file names, and replaces the original only after checking that version.
strings.lock.dialog_html:
{name} is encrypted and read-only.

After unlocking you can add, rename and delete files. Nothing in the archive changes until you click Save.

On Save, Archy:

  • writes a complete new version ({size}) next to the original, which takes about as long as copying the archive,
  • with the same password {names}and without compression, like the original,
  • and replaces the original only after checking the new version. If anything goes wrong or you cancel, the original stays unchanged.

This needs {size} of free space on the same disk for a moment (free now: {free}).
strings.save.extract_busy_text: Saving replaces the archive. Wait until the extraction has finished and save then; your changes stay staged.
strings.save.no_space_text:
When saving, Archy writes a new version next to the original and only then replaces the original. That needs about {needed} of free space on the archive's disk; {free} is free.

Free up some space and try again. Your changes stay staged.

strings.settings.mode_hint.memory: Nothing is written to disk. A file that does not fit in memory cannot be viewed.
strings.settings.mode_hint.overflow: Memory first. What does not fit (a large folder, a large video or PDF) goes to the temporary folder.
strings.settings.mode_hint.disk: The open folder is unpacked to the temporary folder instead of memory, and videos and PDFs play from there. Light on memory, a little slower.
strings.settings.temp_security: Temporary files are always encrypted (AES-256) with a key that exists only in memory. No readable file or file name ever lands on disk, and after quitting or a crash any leftovers are useless.
strings.settings.advanced_hint: Automatic keeps adapting to the free memory. A fixed value is a maximum; what goes beyond it or makes the system too tight goes to disk, encrypted, when temporary files are on, and is skipped otherwise.

strings.settings.changed_restart: The new language applies after you restart Archy.
